scorecards.inningsCommentary: Entering the third innings with the match balance in flux, Bangladesh sought to extend their lead and set a decisive fourth-innings target. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 74 from Mushfiqur Rahim, complemented by a commanding 69-run stand between Mohammad Mahmudullah and Mushfiqur Rahim that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 4.72 RPO. India's bowling response was spearheaded by UT Yadav (6/53), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Bangladesh's total of 195/10 (41.1 ov) closed their second innings, cementing a formidable target and transferring immense pressure onto the opposition.

summaryTab.matchStory: Bangladesh were bowled out for 106/11 in the first innings amidst sustained bowling pressure. India replied strongly with 347/9, powered by Virat Kohli's commanding century (136) to swing the contest. Bangladesh posted 195 in their second innings, shifting match momentum decisively through crucial partnerships.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Eden Gardens commenced with high tactical intensity as Bangladesh posted 106/11 (30.3 ov) in their opening innings. In response, India countered with 347/9 (89.4 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 6-Wicket Spell: UT Yadav (6/53), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Ishant Sharma delivered a masterclass for India (10 Wickets), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (India 61%) and allowing India to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Bangladesh faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. India's bowling unit, bolstered by UT Yadav (9 Wickets), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing India won by innings & 46 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: India's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Bangladesh produced fighting phases, India won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
